courses.title: Advanced Actuarial Mathematics
courses.summary: Life contingencies, multiple-state models and the valuation of insurance and annuity contracts.
courses.overview: The mathematical core of life insurance and pensions. Starting from survival models, the course builds up to pricing and reserving for life insurance and annuity products, then extends to multiple lives, multiple decrements and multiple-state models used for disability and critical-illness cover.
outcomes: Build and interpret survival models and life tables
Value life insurance and annuity benefits using actuarial present values
Calculate premiums and policy reserves, including Thiele's differential equation
Apply multiple-state and multiple-decrement models to real products
topics: Survival models and the force of mortality
Multiple lives, multiple decrements and multiple-state models
courses.prerequisites: Probability, calculus and the theory of interest (financial mathematics).
audience: Actuarial science students in their later undergraduate or postgraduate years
Candidates preparing for professional life-contingencies examinations
Analysts in life insurance and pensions who want a rigorous foundation

courses.title: Advanced Risk Mathematics
courses.summary: Loss distributions, aggregate claims and ruin theory for general insurance.
courses.overview: How general insurers model claims. The course covers fitting loss distributions, modelling claim frequency and severity together as aggregate claims, the effect of reinsurance and policy limits, and ruin theory for assessing an insurer's long-run solvency.
outcomes: Fit and compare loss distributions for claim severity
Model aggregate claims using compound distributions
Quantify the effect of deductibles, limits and reinsurance
Use ruin theory to reason about insurer solvency
courses.prerequisites: Probability and statistics, including common distributions and moment-generating functions.
audience: General insurance pricing and reserving analysts

courses.title: Actuarial Risk Management
courses.summary: Identifying, measuring and managing risk across insurance, pensions and financial institutions.
courses.overview: The practitioner's view of risk. The course connects actuarial techniques to decisions: how institutions identify and classify risks, measure them with modern risk measures, hold capital against them, match assets to liabilities, and govern the whole process under regulation.
outcomes: Identify and classify the risks facing financial institutions
Apply risk measures such as VaR and expected shortfall
Explain approaches to capital, asset-liability management and hedging
Discuss regulation, governance and enterprise risk management
courses.prerequisites: Familiarity with actuarial or financial mathematics is helpful.
audience: Candidates preparing for actuarial risk management examinations

courses.title: Pensions Mathematics
courses.summary: Valuation and funding of defined benefit and defined contribution pension schemes.
courses.overview: The mathematics behind retirement benefits. The course explains how pension schemes are designed, how their liabilities are valued, the funding methods used to set contributions, and how assumptions about salaries, interest and mortality drive the results.
outcomes: Describe defined benefit and defined contribution scheme design
Value pension liabilities using appropriate decrement models
Compare funding methods and set contribution rates
Analyse the effect of assumptions on scheme funding
topics: Valuation of accrued and future benefits
courses.prerequisites: Life contingencies (Advanced Actuarial Mathematics or equivalent).
audience: Consultants working with retirement benefit schemes

courses.title: Advanced Financial Economics
courses.summary: Asset pricing, portfolio theory and derivative valuation for actuaries and financial analysts.
courses.overview: The economic theory that underpins investment and pricing decisions. The course moves from utility and portfolio choice through equilibrium asset pricing models to interest-rate models and the no-arbitrage pricing of options and other derivatives.
outcomes: Apply utility theory and mean-variance portfolio selection
Use CAPM and multifactor models to explain returns
Price derivatives by no-arbitrage and risk-neutral methods
Describe and compare common interest-rate models
courses.prerequisites: Probability, calculus and basic financial mathematics.
audience: Candidates preparing for financial economics examinations

courses.title: Advanced Financial Modelling
courses.summary: Building robust financial models for valuation, forecasting and decision support.
courses.overview: A practical course in building models that decision-makers can trust. It covers model structure, forecasting financial statements, valuation, scenario and sensitivity analysis, and the checks that keep a model accurate and auditable.
outcomes: Structure clear, auditable financial models
Forecast financial statements from sound assumptions
Value businesses and projects using discounted cash flow
Run scenario and sensitivity analysis to support decisions
audience: Analysts in banking, investment and corporate finance

courses.title: Financial Time Series and Econometrics Modelling
courses.summary: Time series and econometric techniques for financial and economic data.
courses.overview: Methods for data that unfold over time. The course covers stationarity and ARIMA models, volatility modelling with ARCH and GARCH, regression and panel econometrics, and forecasting, with applications to markets and macroeconomic data.
outcomes: Test for stationarity and fit ARIMA models
Model time-varying volatility with ARCH and GARCH
Estimate and interpret econometric regression models
Produce and evaluate forecasts
audience: Postgraduate students in finance, economics and statistics
Researchers working with market or macroeconomic data

courses.title: Stochastic Processes Modelling
courses.summary: Markov chains, Poisson processes and Brownian motion with actuarial and financial applications.
courses.overview: The language of randomness over time. The course develops Markov chains, counting processes, continuous-time Markov models and Brownian motion, and shows how they model insurance claims, health states, epidemics and asset prices.
outcomes: Classify stochastic processes and their properties
Analyse discrete- and continuous-time Markov chains
Model claim arrivals with Poisson and counting processes
Use Brownian motion and simple stochastic calculus in finance
topics: Applications in insurance, health and finance
audience: Researchers modelling risk, health or epidemics

courses.title: Statistical Machine Learning & Data Analytics
courses.summary: Supervised and unsupervised learning methods for prediction and insight from data.
courses.overview: Machine learning grounded in statistics. The course covers the full workflow, from preparing data through regression, classification, tree-based ensembles and clustering, to validating models properly so they generalise to new data.
outcomes: Prepare and explore data for modelling
Build regression and classification models
Use tree-based ensembles and clustering methods
Evaluate models with cross-validation and appropriate metrics
topics: Decision trees, random forests and boosting
courses.prerequisites: Introductory statistics; some programming experience helps.
audience: Students in statistics, actuarial science and data science
Researchers applying machine learning to their data

courses.title: Statistical Modelling
courses.summary: Generalised linear models and statistical inference for real-world data.
courses.overview: The core toolkit for drawing conclusions from data. The course reviews estimation and hypothesis testing, then develops linear and generalised linear models for continuous, count and binary outcomes, with careful attention to diagnostics and interpretation.
outcomes: Estimate parameters and test hypotheses correctly
Fit and interpret linear regression models
Use generalised linear models for counts and binary data
Check model assumptions with diagnostics

courses.title: Research and Data Analysis
courses.summary: Research design, data collection and analysis for theses, projects and policy work.
courses.overview: A guide from research question to defended findings. The course covers research design, sampling and data collection, choosing and running the right quantitative analysis, and presenting results clearly in theses, reports and policy briefs.
outcomes: Design a sound research study around a clear question
Choose sampling and data collection methods
Select and run appropriate quantitative analyses
Report findings clearly for academic and policy audiences
audience: Master's and PhD candidates preparing theses
